item.title: XP Founder Urges Brazil to Fix Deficit as Election Debate Looms
item.description: Guilherme Benchimol, the founder and chairman of brokerage firm XP Inc., has a warning: A meaningful fiscal overhaul is essential if the country is to bring interest rates down and create a better environment for investing.

item.title: Azimut Fund Manager Bets on Japanese Bonds as Yields Surge
item.description: Japanese government bonds offer investors one of the best opportunities in global fixed income despite being viewed as high risk, according to an Azimut Group fund manager.

item.title: Trump Latest Tariffs on 60 Economies Face New Legal Challenges: Big Take Podcast
item.description: Economists agree the Section 301 tariffs are designed to hold up under scrutiny.

item.title: Angola Raises $321 Million Through Nation’s Biggest IPO
item.description: Angola has raised 300.3 billion kwanzas ($321 million) through the sale of 15% stake in state-owned wireless operator Unitel SA, marking the southwest African nation’s biggest initial public offering.

item.title: Orange, Morrison Partner on French Data Center Project
item.description: Orange SA and infrastructure manager Morrison are joining forces to create a data center company in France in an effort to strengthen Europe’s digital sovereignty.

item.title: What Is Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 Model and Why Is It Making Waves?
item.description: Chinese startup Moonshot AI’s new artificial-intelligence model has drawn global attention since its release for its powerful capabilities. Now, Moonshot has made the technology available for public download, a step expected to expand the company’s influence at a time when there is growing US concern about China’s rapid strides in AI development.

item.title: Macquarie Sees Oil Glut Risk on US-Iran Deal Before Midterms
item.description: Oil markets could tilt back into oversupply before the end of the year as Washington faces mounting pressure to end the Iran conflict with fewer than 100 days until the midterm elections, analysts from Macquarie Ltd said.

item.title: Philips Lifts Margin Outlook After Getting US Tariff Refund
item.description: Royal Philips NV raised its profitability expectations for 2026 after a US tariff refund bolstered earnings in the second quarter.

item.title: AI Tools Uncover Record Software Flaws in Tech Sector, Database Shows
item.description: The number of software security flaws discovered in popular technology products in 2026 is on pace to roughly double the tally of vulnerabilities that surfaced in 2025, an explosion driven by increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems.

item.title: JPMorgan Sees S&P 500 Poised to Rally as New Buy Signal Flashes
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s analysts said an in-house indicator is “now flashing a buy-signal” — something that has typically indicated the S&P 500 Index is poised to gain.

item.title: Carlyle’s Bansal Says Bonds Shed Role as Stocks’ Shock Absorber
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc.’s asset-backed finance chief said traditional fixed income is losing its reliability as a portfolio shock absorber because those investments are becoming increasingly correlated with stocks.

item.title: Italy Cuts Diesel Tax and Seeks EU Fiscal Room for Energy Aid
item.description: Italy approved a temporary tax cut on diesel fuel through Aug. 6 as the government seeks to cushion the impact of surging energy prices following the widening of the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Peru: Keiko Fujimori Names Elmer Cuba as Peru Finance Minister
item.description: Consultant and former central bank director Elmer Cuba will lead Peruvian President-elect Keiko Fujimori’s economic agenda, a technocratic pick seen as signaling macroeconomic continuity in one of Latin America’s most stable economies.

item.title: Muni Bonds Look Cheapest Since March After Rough Week of Returns
item.description: US state and local government debt hit its cheapest level since the spring, after inflation fears caused municipal bonds to see their worst week of returns since April 2025.

item.title: Paschi, Banco BPM Advisers Working on Deal With Cash Component
item.description: Advisers for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA and Banco BPM SpA’s are in talks over a possible merger of equals, structured as a mix of shares and cash, as an alternative to Intesa Sanpaolo SpA’s €35 billion ($40 billion) bid for Monte Paschi, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Oil Startup Backed by Ex-Goldman Commodity Chief Currie to IPO
item.description: Jeff Currie, the former Goldman Sachs Group Inc. commodities chief whose calls made him one of Wall Street’s best-known energy market strategists, is preparing to raise £50 million ($67 million) in a London stock market listing to build an oil producer in the Gulf of Mexico.

item.title: TPG Is Said in Talks to Buy Netrality for Up to $3 Billion
item.description: TPG Inc. is in exclusive talks to acquire Macquarie Group Ltd.-backed Netrality Data Centers, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Venezuela Creditor Group Expands Ahead of Debt Restructuring
item.description: A group of Venezuela bondholders is adding new members as it positions for long-awaited debt talks over what could be the biggest sovereign restructuring in more than a decade.

item.title: The Four Words Everyone in Tech Should Say
item.description: Lina Khan was right.

item.title: LVMH Fashion Unit’s Return to Growth Held Back by Iran War
item.description: LVMH’s key fashion and leather goods unit, home to Louis Vuitton and Dior, barely eked out sales growth last quarter as the conflict in the Middle East deterred wealthy shoppers.

item.title: Jersey Mike’s IPO Said to Be More Than 10 Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Jersey Mike’s Subs Inc.’s initial public offering has attracted investor demand for more than 10 times the available shares ahead of pricing on Wednesday, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Southern Africa Payments Hub Eyes More Currencies to Boost Trade
item.description: A multibillion-dollar cross-border payments platform serving southern Africa plans to expand beyond the South African rand and Angolan kwanza, widening the range of currencies it supports to lower transaction costs and boost trade.

item.title: Amazon Seeks FCC Nod to Beam Satellite Coverage to Mobile Phones
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has requested permission from the US Federal Communications Commission to launch a direct-to-device network of 5,000 satellites to provide mobile services to cell phones from space, furthering the company’s competition with SpaceX.

item.title: Tyson, JBS Shares Surge as US Reopens Mexico Cattle Imports After Screwworm Ban
item.description: Shares of meatpackers Tyson Foods Inc. and JBS NV surged after the US said it would resume cattle shipments from Mexico, easing a domestic shortage that has led to higher costs for their animals.

item.title: Corporate Bonds Lose Appeal as Shock Absorber, Carlyle Says
item.description: As corporate bonds become less reliable at protecting against market shocks, investors are looking to asset-backed finance as an alternative source of stability, according to Carlyle Group.

item.title: ASML Slides on Report of China Starting DUV Tool Production
item.description: ASML Holding NV shares slid to the lowest since early June after a report that a Chinese state-backed company has begun mass producing certain chipmaking machines, posing a potential threat to the Dutch firm’s sales.

item.title: Citi Traders Are Betting Fed Will Keep Rates on Hold This Week
item.description: Citigroup Inc.’s traders are betting the Federal Reserve will leave rates unchanged this week, even as the swap markets assign a more than one-in-three chance of a quarter-point hike.

item.title: Nvidia Credit Risk Jumps in Swaps Market on AI Deal Talk Reports
item.description: The cost of protecting Nvidia Corp.’s debt against default surged by the most on record on Monday after reports that the chipmaker is in conversations on more than $750 billion of artificial intelligence infrastructure deals, stoking fears that the company is taking on even more obligations.

item.title: Robeco’s $18 Billion Stock Picker Bets on Argentina After Hiatus
item.description: It took nearly a decade for one of Europe’s biggest emerging-market investors to return to Argentine stocks.

item.title: Biggest State Street Debate Is Where Bessent Bond Gauge Goes
item.description: The most involved discussion at State Street Corp.’s $6 trillion investment-management arm is around the outlook for 10-year US Treasury yields — the main financial metric targeted by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
